newsitem.title: CHINA: Strong quake rocks remote China region.
newsitem.headline: Strong quake rocks remote China region.

text.p: A strong earthquake measuring 7.1 on the Richter scale hit a sparsely populated area in China's northwestern region of Xinjiang on Tuesday, a seismological official said.
The earthquake rocked the Kunlun mountains at 1044 GMT, the official said by telephone.
The seismological bureau had received no immediate reports of casualties or damage, he said.
"There are very few people living in that area," the official said.
The epicentre of the quake appeared to be near one of the areas where China and India clashed in their brief border war in 1962.
A resident in Hotan, some 250 km (150 miles) from the epicentre, told Reuters by telephone that a slight tremor was felt but there was no damage.
Chinese experts say the country is experiencing a period of intense seismological activity that will last until the end of the century.
A total of 50 earthquakes measuring more than five on the Richter scale hit China in 1995, an increase of 18.5 percent from the year before, according to official figures.
